newsitem.title: USA: Oxford has higher quarter on increased enrollment.
newsitem.headline: Oxford has higher quarter on increased enrollment.

text.p: Oxford Health Plans Inc. said Tuesday its first-quarter earnings rose 86 percent, primarily due to increased enrollment in the company's fully insured programmes.
Oxford said its profits rose to $34.4 million, or 42 cents per share, from $18.5 million, or 25 cents per share, in the prior year's first quarter.
Revenues for the first quarter ended March 31 reached $987.3 million, a 50 percent increase from $658.10 million a year ago.

Oxford's enrollment totalled approximately 1,738,800 members at March 31, an increase of over 200,000 during the first quarter of 1997 and almost 45 percent higher than the membership at the end of last year's first quarter.
Almost all of the new membership has come from fully insured enrollment, which has continued to grow in the second quarter of 1997, the company said.

Oxford administers health maintenance organisations, point-of service plans, third-party administration of employer funded benefit plans, Medicare and Medicaid plans, and dental plans. It markets its health plans to employers in New York, New Jersey, Pennsylvania, Connecticut and New Hampshire.
Oxford's stock gained $2.625 to $67.125 in morning trading on Nasdaq.
